what: An Atmos playback device on the machine, and what it can and cannot settle

device.sink: TCL TS8132 soundbar, seen over HDMI as EP-HDMI-RX
device.path: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER HDMI audio endpoint

what_it_advertises.method: the audio data block of its EDID CEA extension, read from the registry
what_it_advertises.reading: it takes both formats this project decodes as bitstreams, so a TrueHD Atmos or a Dolby Digital Plus Atmos stream can be sent to it whole

what_it_could_settle: whether an independent renderer opens the object presentation of the three titles Dolby's software refuses at presentation 16. If it does, the refusal is a property of that software rather than of the streams, which is the open question.
whether it renders the configuration 0 stream Dolby's software gives six channels for.
what_it_cannot_do: give a machine-readable answer. A sink reports what it decoded on its own display and nowhere else: there is no return path for that over HDMI. So every reading is a person looking at the front panel, which makes it a yes/no observation rather than a per-object measurement.
how: mpv --audio-device='wasapi/{8ff19f11-40c5-4444-9762-490395ddb6b1}' --audio-exclusive=yes --audio-spdif=truehd --no-video --start=<a loud passage> --length=20 <file>, and --audio-spdif=eac3 for the Dolby Digital Plus streams
status: prepared, not run: the reading needs a person at the device
